channel.title: Noticias del Mundo — Ciencia
channel.description: Noticias de ciencia de todas las fuentes configuradas.

item.title: Sending an Australian astronaut to space is expensive. How do we work out if it's worth it?
item.description: Australia is currently in talks with the European Space Agency (ESA) over potentially flying Katherine Bennell-Pegg on a future space mission. If accepted, Bennell-Pegg—who is the director of space technology at the Australian Space Agency and completed ESA training in 2024—would become the first officially funded Australian astronaut. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New eyes in the sky make timber harvesting and forest conservation easier and more efficient
item.description: Flying thousands of feet above northern and eastern Maine, Dave Sandilands searched for illegally dumped trash. On behalf of the New England Forestry Foundation, the University of Maine pilot was surveying both the 760,000-acre (308,000-hectare) Pingree Easement in northern Maine, home to the state's most productive peregrine falcon nesting area, and 335,000 acres (136,000 hectares) in Washington County through the Downeast Lakes Forestry Partnership. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nasa's asteroid crash test left stadium-sized crater; first images reveal
item.description: Images from the ESA's Hera spacecraft show the aftermath of NASA's successful impact on asteroid Dimorphos. The DART mission altered the asteroid's orbit significantly, demonstrating the potential for planetary defense strategies. Hera's observations offer vital insights into how deflection methods could work in the future. The collision created a crater, providing scientists with important data on the effects of such impacts. Publicado también por: BBC News - World. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Las imágenes del asteroide seleccionado para poner a prueba las defensas de la Tierra revelan un cráter del tamaño de un estadio
item.description: La superficie del asteroide se transformó después de que una nave espacial se estrellara deliberadamente contra él hace cuatro años. Fuente: BBC News Mundo.

item.title: Scientists discover mysterious lakes more than a mile beneath the Red Sea
item.description: More than a mile beneath the surface of the Red Sea, scientists have discovered rare underwater lakes that could reveal secrets about Earth's ancient oceans and the possibility of alien life. Known as brine pools, these extremely salty, oxygen-free environments are surprisingly teeming with microbial life, challenging our understanding of where living organisms can survive. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Do we really know more about space than the ocean?
item.description: New discoveries are made about the world every day—a species of deep-sea fish here, a new galaxy there. There's a saying, "We know more about space than the ocean." But is this true? How do we determine knowing? Is it the number of things we have directly observed, or is it a matter of resolution? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Astronomers may have discovered a black hole born before the first stars
item.description: A mysterious object named Phoebe, detected when it briefly magnified a distant star, could be a primordial black hole formed just after the Big Bang. With an estimated mass only three times that of the Moon, it may be a 13-billion-year-old cosmic relic that offers new clues to the mystery of dark matter. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: From solving to 'digesting': How mathematicians can adapt to the dramatic changes AI has brought to their field
item.description: Mathematics is having an existential crisis. On Nov. 20, 2026, a mathematician at the AI company Anthropic claimed that while working with the model Claude, he had solved the generalized Riemann hypothesis, the most famous problem in mathematics. This problem has stood unsolved for 167 years, and solving it could easily warrant a Fields Medal—considered equivalent to a Nobel Prize, but for mathematics. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: World’s largest trial of robotic knee replacement reveals surprising results
item.description: Robot-assisted knee replacement surgery offers greater surgical precision, but a landmark clinical trial has revealed a surprising limitation. Despite the advanced technology, patients experienced no meaningful improvements in pain, mobility, or recovery compared with conventional surgery after one year. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Dinosaurs likely tore meat like birds of prey
item.description: Meat-eating dinosaurs probably fed by dragging their teeth backward through flesh like a saw rather than biting straight down like a dagger, new experiments suggest. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Disliking AI doesn't deter its influence
item.description: An aversion to artificial intelligence (AI) does not lessen the influence of the technology on people and their decision-making, according to new research from City St George's, University of London. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Children in overcrowded homes get poorer GCSE results, study finds
item.description: Researchers urge ministers to ensure young people in rented homes have space for a desk in their bedroom Children who share a bedroom and lack a quiet place to study at home get worse GCSE results than their peers, according to a major report on how poor housing affects education. The research, carried out by leading academics at University College London for the Sutton Trust, a social mobility charity, urged UK ministers to ensure all young people in rented accommodation have space for a desk. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Murray Social affairs correspondent

item.title: Sweden tops global media freedom support rankings as international funding declines
item.description: Sweden has been ranked the world's leading supporter of international media freedom, according to a new index. The index also highlights a decline in funding from 30 leading donor countries, despite growing threats to independent journalism worldwide. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Giant deer bones may push human arrival in Ireland back by 1,000 years
item.description: A team of archaeologists and scientists has uncovered tantalizing new evidence that Late Upper Paleolithic hunter-gatherers may have lived in southern Ireland around 13,500 years ago—nearly a millennium earlier than currently confirmed. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fermented milk may have held ritual power in Neolithic Denmark
item.description: Experimental archaeology sheds light on the substances fermented in Neolithic Scandinavian pottery and deposited in tombs, suggesting fermented dairy products held symbolic significance in prehistoric funerary rituals. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists discover a surprising twist in how the body burns calories
item.description: Researchers have discovered that a drug can significantly increase the body's energy expenditure without clearly activating calorie-burning brown fat. The unexpected finding reveals a new challenge in developing obesity treatments that harness the body's natural fat-burning machinery. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Minecraft-like DNA cubes self-assemble into complex 3D nanostructures
item.description: Associate professor Petr Sulc and his research team have developed a programmable DNA-based building system that could open new possibilities for nanorobots, three-dimensional electronics and next-generation nanotechnology. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Draining peatlands leaves a long legacy of warming
item.description: Peatland ecosystems like bogs and swamps perform an important balancing act: Their vegetation takes up huge amounts of carbon dioxide, while their soil microbes produce methane. Although methane is a potent greenhouse gas, peatlands exhibit a net cooling effect on the planet because of the sheer scale of carbon dioxide they remove from the atmosphere, which has amounted to hundreds of gigatons globally over thousands of years. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Stabilizing atomically thin metals with sandwich structures: Machine learning expands the search
item.description: Atomically thin metals, metallenes, are promising materials for catalysis, electronics and energy conversion, but their synthesis has been challenging. Researchers from the University of Jyväskylä have now identified more than 300 stable metallene sandwich structures using machine learning and high-performance computing. The results provide researchers with a practical roadmap for the fabrication of new two-dimensional metals. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Certain fungi turn specialized plant cells into water-carrying cells using one protein
item.description: Can a pathogen that causes damage to a plant also make that plant more resilient to drought? An international research team led by the University of Göttingen has investigated this apparent paradox. The researchers discovered how certain fungi promote the formation of new water-conducting cells in plants. At the same time, infected plants showed increased tolerance to drought stress. The results were published in the journal Cell Host & Microbe. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Carbon nanotube measurements reveal quantum model better explains collective electron behavior
item.description: An international team of scientists from Lithuania, Finland and Israel has conducted both theoretical and experimental research into carbon nanotubes, becoming the first to demonstrate which physical model governs the motion and interactions of electrons within them. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Five reasons why we should still make things with our hands
item.description: It's 7 a.m. Still dark outside. "Alex, time to wake up! You have a busy day ahead, with an important meeting at 8:30," announces the alarm in a soft but firm voice. Alex wakes up immediately, already thinking about the presentation that still needs a few finishing touches. In the kitchen, the coffee machine, set up for 7 a.m. sharp, has just finished brewing. "Alexa, set the temperature to 20 degrees," says Alex, reaching for the coffee. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New photos reveal stadium-sized crater in asteroid knocked off course by NASA
item.description: A spacecraft observing the asteroid will approach within 13km of it next month, obtaining increasingly higher-resolution images. Fuente: ABC News Australia.

item.title: New inhibitor restores antibiotic activity against drug-resistant bacteria
item.description: Researchers from Imperial College London and collaborators have identified a potent small-molecule inhibitor that can restore the activity of the antibiotic ciprofloxacin against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA's Europa Clipper zooming by Earth on way to Jupiter's icy moon
item.description: NASA's Europa Clipper will soon swing past Earth before making a yearslong beeline for Jupiter, where the orbiter will probe whether the ocean beneath its moon Europa's icy shell has the ingredients for life. The flyby will offer a propellant-saving boost and an opportunity to prepare for the science-gathering that lies ahead. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Shopping as a 'collector' makes us want to buy more, new research shows
item.description: Shoppers are more likely to buy products and pay more for them when they adopt a "collecting mindset," according to new research co-authored by Bayes Business School (City St George's, University of London). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Giant lambda-shaped stellar nursery found in the Milky Way's outskirts
item.description: Massive stars often form in dense regions, called "hubs," where filamentary structures made of star-forming materials meet. These star-forming complexes are "hub-filament" systems. Astronomers have discovered one such large network of molecular gas filaments in the outer regions of the Milky Way. It is called the λ-complex, and the structure is bigger than most known hub-filament systems. The research paper was published in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society on Nov. 17. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Moment Nasa spacecraft hit asteroid - and what happened next
item.description: The crash was "like something out of a disaster movie", the BBC's science editor Rebecca Morelle says. Fuente: BBC News - World.

item.title: Siempre nos han dicho que parar 15 minutos a hacer ejercicio mejora el estudio. La ciencia dice que no es tan sencillo
item.description: Cuando nos ponemos a estudiar delante de un tocho de apuntes, es fácil que al rato la concentración comience a flaquear. En este caso, levantarse de la silla para hacer 15 minutos de ejercicio moderado es algo que siempre nos han dicho que puede despejarnos y mejorar el rendimiento académico. El problema es que no es tan fácil. La base. Uno de los pilares habituales para defender los descansos activos viene de un ensayo publicado en 2014 . En este un grupo de investigadores evaluó a 123 niños de entre 10 y 11 años de cuatro colegios de primaria tras hacer una hora de deberes. De este modo… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: José A. Lizana

item.title: Sustainable procurement in multinational corporations depends on people and the operating environment
item.description: Elizabeth Jeromaa's doctoral dissertation in management, to be examined at the University of Vaasa, demonstrates that it is possible for companies to implement environmentally sustainable procurement practices, though there is no one-size-fits-all model. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Heaven scent: Study shows link between a partner's body odor and sexual intimacy
item.description: Many people spend a considerable amount of time and money trying to disguise their natural body odor. But not everyone finds our natural scent unpleasant. In fact, it could be part of what makes a couple click. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Using lunar craters as free radiation shields for moon base nuclear reactors
item.description: Powering any future lunar base is a massive engineering challenge. The two-week lunar night can drain batteries charged by solar panels during the two-week day, if the batteries themselves can even withstand the freezing temperatures that go along with it. So, for decades at this point, engineers have planned to use a nuclear reactor to at least partially power any future human settlement on the moon. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Simulations reveal how a solar vortex and reconnecting magnetic fields can launch a rotating jet
item.description: Solar spicules are slender jets commonly found in the chromosphere. They lift relatively cool plasma from the lower solar atmosphere, carry energy upward, and in some cases rotate as they evolve. Small-scale vortices also occur frequently between convection-driven granules in the photosphere. Two questions remain incompletely answered: how these photospheric vortices help form spicules, and how much mass and energy the rising jets carry into the corona. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Structural agility of 2D crystals enables digital doping of graphene superlattices
item.description: A study published in Nature has demonstrated that applying an electric field can switch the atomic arrangement in a stack of two-dimensional (2D) crystals, accompanied by an unusual charge behavior. This provides a new experimental platform for exploring how the structural and electronic properties of atomically thin materials interact. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Enhances Supplier Program, Announces Mentor-Protégé Agreement
item.description: How NASA works with small businesses is evolving, and as a result, the agency is strengthening the domestic aerospace industrial base to support future exploration missions through its recently renamed Small Business Supplier Development Program. As part of the program, NASA announced its latest Mentor-Protégé Agreement, this one signed between The Boeing Company and GRACE […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer M. Dooren

item.title: Uterine pressure guides head-to-tail axis formation in mouse embryos
item.description: During animal development, the establishment of the three primary body axes—head-to-tail (anterior-posterior), dorsal-ventral and left-right—is essential for building a proper body structure. A fertilized egg, initially a single cell, undergoes repeated cell divisions to form a multicellular structure called an embryo, and body axes are formed within the embryo. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Weak oversight and financial incentives may fuel health care corruption, review finds
item.description: Corruption in health systems may arise when governance failures offer opportunities and systemic vulnerabilities provide incentives for private gain, according to an umbrella review published in the open-access journal PLOS Global Public Health by Michele Coleman and Petra Varkonyi from the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, United Kingdom, and colleagues. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The triple helix: How a rare twist in human evolution may influence fetal cooling
item.description: The human umbilical cord is an evolutionary rarity, with the arrangement of blood vessels within its distinctive twisted structure potentially helping unborn babies stay cool in the womb, according to a team led by University of Manchester and University of Southampton scientists. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Mapping the uncharted plate tectonic cycle: The hidden path from plate destruction to new oceanic crust
item.description: Since the discovery of plate tectonics, the ultimate fate of the massive plates that sink into Earth's interior mantle at subduction zones has remained a major geological quest. Meanwhile, magma continuously rises from the deep mantle to form new oceanic crust, erupting as mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORB). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New England's summer thunderstorms grow shorter and heavier, raising flash flood risk
item.description: A growing share of New England's summer rain is falling in the form of heavy, heat-related showers and thunderstorms, raising the risk of flash flooding events across the region as the climate continues to warm. That's according to a new study by Brown University researchers published in Science Advances. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Errors in judging friendships predict who will connect or drift apart six months later
item.description: Decades of research show that mental representations of social networks are riddled with errors, with people commonly misidentifying existing ties and reporting relationships that do not exist. While these inaccuracies have been interpreted as noise arising from the limits of memory or attention, Brown University researchers have discovered a much more intriguing explanation: These "errors" are accurate representations of social connections that just haven't happened yet. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Evolution's balancing act—keeping genes in sync after genome duplication
item.description: Getting the right balance is important in all walks of life, whether it's a healthy combination of food groups in a balanced diet or a balanced mix of skills that allows a work or sports team to succeed. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The birds are listening: Seabirds reveal hidden fishing activity at sea
item.description: Researchers from the University of Oxford fitted miniature audio recorders and GPS trackers to seabirds to better understand the impacts of fishing boats on wildlife. This revealed that seabirds may be interacting with human vessels considerably more than official tracking data suggest. The results have been published on Nov. 25 in Science Advances. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Antidiscrimination laws in US often lack clear wording relevant to multiracial identities
item.description: A new analysis highlights the limited appearance of the phrases "perceived race" and "multiracial" in U.S. federal and state antidiscrimination laws and demonstrates how court cases can be analyzed to explore whether such wording contributes to ambiguity that may hamper equal protection of multiracial people. Victoria Jackson and colleagues at Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health, U.S., present these findings in the journal PLOS One on Nov. 25, 2026. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Global ocean iodine won't offset future air pollution, study warns
item.description: The world's oceans will not play the role of scrubbing harmful ozone pollution from the atmosphere as the planet warms in the way that was expected, new research suggests. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA's Hubble views ocean of stars in groundwork for Roman
item.description: An expanse of stars gleams in a rainbow of colors in these NASA Hubble Space Telescope images of the Milky Way. The images focus on an area of sky toward the galactic bulge, a densely packed, spherical region of stars that surrounds the center of a galaxy's disk. These Hubble observations are part of a survey that will help researchers better interpret upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope observations as they seek to characterize the stars and search for exoplanets in this busy region of our galaxy. Publicado también por: NASA. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Only one in five of Kazakhstan's endemic plants has data for initial range screening
item.description: Kazakhstan has hundreds of plant species found nowhere else in the world. Many have been known to botanists for decades, described in floristic publications and held in herbarium collections. Yet knowing that a plant exists is different from having the information needed to judge its prospects for survival. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Eyes Crop Candidates for Future Menus
item.description: As NASA prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition, and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can help with menus in deep space, something top of mind this week as the nation celebrates Thanksgiving. Recent testing points to strawberries, […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Childhood, Career Come Full Circle for Budget Analyst at NASA Goddard
item.description: Conversations about NASA were the norm around the dinner table during Ashley Knight’s childhood. Her parents worked at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland, and discussions about happenings at the agency continued even when they came home from the office. “I remember a poignant dialogue we had after the space shuttle Challenger disaster,” […] Fuente: NASA.
item.dc:creator: Rob Garner

item.title: NASA’s Hubble Views Ocean of Stars in Groundwork for Roman
item.description: These Hubble observations are part of a survey that will help researchers better interpret upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope observations as they seek to characterize the stars and search for exoplanets in this busy region of our galaxy. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Genetic analysis reveals peak orchid root fungal diversity at one of the most biodiverse places on Earth
item.description: The fungal communities living in the roots of epiphytic orchids vary with altitude, location and orchid species, according to research published in the journal Microbial Ecology. The study, conducted in Podocarpus National Park in southern Ecuador, found that mid-elevation forests harbor the greatest diversity of these microorganisms, while their richness decreases at higher elevations and their community composition differs. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: La revelación de Reid Wiseman, comandante de Artemis II, al hablar de las próximas misiones de la NASA
item.description: Tras su regreso a la Tierra, Donald Trump le entregó a cada tripulante una medalla Medalla de Honor Espacial del Congreso, durante una ceremonia en el Centro Espacial Jonhson de Houston; qué dijo el astronauta Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: How utilities, communities can help build resilience for vulnerable families during power outages
item.description: For low-income households, extended power outages can create devastating losses of food and money, as well as feelings of comfort and security within their homes, according to research led by the University of Michigan. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Board diversity and digital readiness linked to corporate adaptability during pandemic
item.description: Think "pandemic" and the word "pivot" is not far behind. What happened to organizational communications during COVID-19, though, was an unprecedented sea change. For businesses trying to stay connected to investors like pension and mutual funds, in-person roadshows, brokerage-hosted conferences and "analyst day" meetings were adapted into virtual versions filtered through the safety of personal digital devices as everyone hunkered down at home. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ant rivalry temporarily protects native ants until one invader takes over
item.description: When an invasive species enters a natural habitat, it can start competing for resources with native species and threaten their survival. If more than one invasive species occupies the same habitat, the interactions between them can further contribute to the damage and disruption that ensues. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Japan unveils rover prototype for moon water mission
item.description: Japan's space agency unveiled Wednesday a test model of a rover that will travel to the moon's south pole in a search for water, which could potentially be used for rocket fuel. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: China launches Shenzhou 24 spacecraft carrying 2 Chinese and 1 Pakistani astronaut
item.description: China on Wednesday launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft with three astronauts—two Chinese and a Pakistani—sending the first foreign crew member to its space station. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Common sleep and anxiety drugs could be harming aging brains
item.description: Nearly one in three older adults with dementia or other cognitive disorders takes potentially harmful medications that can worsen brain function and increase the risk of hospitalization and premature death. Despite encouraging progress over the past decade, researchers warn that medication-related harm remains a major and potentially preventable threat to healthy aging. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Peppermint oil significantly lowers blood pressure in just 20 days
item.description: Peppermint oil may have a surprisingly powerful effect on blood pressure. In a randomized study of 40 adults, researchers found that taking small doses twice daily for 20 days lowered systolic blood pressure by an average of 8.5 mmHg. Those receiving a placebo experienced no significant improvement. The discovery points to a promising, low-cost natural approach to managing mildly elevated blood pressure. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A space telescope hunting for dark matter just discovered something unexpected
item.description: ESA’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, despite being designed to study distant galaxies and the mysteries of the dark Universe. The icy object is approximately 1.3 billion kilometers from Earth and follows an unusual orbit that takes thousands of years to complete. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: China ya tiene fecha para sacar agua y oxígeno de la Luna: 2030
item.description: Aunque la NASA está haciendo mucho más ruido en lo referente a su carrera particular hacia la Luna , China también está en la lid, pisándole los talones. La agencia espacial estadounidense espera volver a pisar la Luna en 2028, con su misión Artemis IV. China es más cautelosa y habla de antes de 2030, pero no da un año exacto. Para lo que sí ha dado un año, precisamente 2030, es para comenzar a extraer materiales de nuestro satélite. La extracción de recursos será esencial para que en el futuro los humanos puedan alargar sus estancias allí. Por eso, lo que acaba de anunciar el diseñador jefe… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

item.title: Physicists trap antimatter in a breakthrough that could explain why the universe exists
item.description: Positrons are the antimatter counterpart of an electron. Physicists trapped a positron and cooled it to temperatures near absolute zero. Positron is suspended in a wall-free trap, safely separated from ordinary matter. Team will conduct most precise comparison yet between matter and antimatter. Any difference between the electron and positron could expose cracks in the Standard Model of particle physics. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: NBA star Kevin Durant lists Arizona mansion for $13.9 million, a year after trade to Houston
item.description: Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant has listed his sprawling Arizona property for $13.9 million—just three years after he picked up the palatial pad. Fuente: MarketWatch.

item.title: Not everything that sounds plausible works: Testing ideas to win support for carbon pricing
item.description: What makes people support a carbon price? To find out, 108 researchers, led by a research team at the University of Innsbruck, Austria, tested 55 different ideas at the same time, from information campaigns to reflection tasks. On average, there was a small but statistically significant positive effect. Individually, the effect was detectable for only 11 of the 55 ideas. One of the strongest effects came from writing a letter to a fictional person of a future generation. The results were recently published in the journal Nature Human Behaviour. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What is a thought made of? Why human consciousness may be beyond AI’s reach
item.description: A new theory suggests that the brain may chemically encode and retrieve memories rather than relying solely on electrical signals. Researchers propose that interactions between brain cells and their molecular surroundings could help explain the intimate connection between memory, emotion, and thought. Their findings challenge the assumption that increasingly powerful computers could eventually develop human-like consciousness. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: La selección, a tomar Montenegro, el pequeño país de los gigantes
item.description: Segundo en el mundo por estatura media (1,83), la extraordinaria complexión física de sus hombres, por genética, dieta y geografía, le ayuda a brillar en el deporte   Fuente: Marca.
item.dc:creator: Jesús Sánchez

item.title: Houston, we have a problem: NASA chief fires back at Marjorie Taylor Greene's Moon landing denial
item.description: Greene's post denying the Moon landing came after NASA shared an announcement that it had mobilized specialized research aircraft to support federal government operations in Iowa Fuente: The Jerusalem Post - International.
item.dc:creator: BY SHIR PERETS

item.title: China launches crewed spaceship carrying first Pakistani astronaut to its space station
item.description: Using a Long March-2F rocket, the spacecraft took ‌off at 8:18 a.m. (0018 GMT) ‌from ⁠the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre ⁠in northwest China Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: China sends first foreign astronaut to its space station as Pakistani joins Shenzhou 24 crew
item.description: Nature, Published online: 24 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03829-y Muhammad Zeeshan Ali is flying this week to the Tiangong module aboard a Chinese spacecraft. Publicado también por: The Jerusalem Post - International, Nature. Fuente: Euronews.

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 25 – SPHEREx Seeing Through Dust
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 25 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. To view this […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Georgia’s Pecan Belt
item.description: Since an early-1900s planting boom, orchards along the Flint River in southwest Georgia have become a center of U.S. pecan production. Fuente: NASA.

item.title: New EU Bureaucracy Index: EU law has more than doubled since 2010
item.description: The new EU Bureaucracy Index measures the volume of EU law in force, and it shows a record high: At the end of 2025, the EU regulations and directives in force comprised around 47,600 standard pages, 118% more than in 2010. The volume of EU law has thus more than doubled in 15 years, and it continued to grow in 2025. The main drivers are sanctions regulations and new sets of rules in environmental, consumer and health law. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Stanford scientists discover 3 hidden brain types behind ADHD and anxiety
item.description: An AI-powered analysis of thousands of children's brain scans has revealed three distinct brain types underlying ADHD and anxiety that do not neatly fit traditional diagnoses. These hidden biological patterns can appear before a diagnosis is made, potentially enabling earlier detection and more effective, personalized treatments. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: China's Shenzhou-24 space flight takes off with Pakistani national as first foreign astronaut
item.description: China is promoting the Tiangong space station as a hub for international cooperation while the NASA-led International Space Station faces possible retirement by 2030. Publicado también por: The Hindu - International. Fuente: The Jerusalem Post - International.
item.dc:creator: BY REUTERS

item.title: A star's 'obliquity' likely has little impact on a given planet's habitability
item.description: A star's axial tilt as it relates to the circumstellar disk that surrounds it is known as stellar obliquity. Over space and time, there are a myriad of solar-type stars with all sorts of obliquities. But the question heretofore has always been what effect a given star's initial obliquity has on the planetary system that forms around it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: What draws data centers to a community?
item.description: As Oklahoma communities weigh new data center development, research co-authored by a University of Oklahoma architecture professor offers insight into what draws major technology companies to locations—and why those choices matter locally. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Physicists just sent an unblockable message through a brick wall using gravity
item.description: Scientists have successfully transmitted a message through a brick wall using nothing but gravity, an old elevator, and an incredibly sensitive detector. By moving a massive counterweight between two positions, researchers encoded the word "Gravity" into tiny changes in gravitational pull. Unlike Wi-Fi or radio signals, gravity passes through ordinary barriers without being blocked, offering a potentially revolutionary way to communicate. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Consistent friendship groups linked to longer lives in dolphin populations
item.description: Researchers analysed 40 years of data on a population of around 400 wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins living in the eastern gulf of Shark Bay. Fuente: ABC News Australia.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Clarke

item.title: Ultrathin 'rainbow' sails could power spacecraft and shade the Earth
item.description: For years, whimsically minded space enthusiasts have been dreaming of sailing across the vastness of the void on beams of sunlight. Photons, the massless particles that make up those beams of sunlight, still carry momentum and can therefore impart a gentle push when they bounce off a surface. This force is the concept behind "solar sailing," which has been having a bit of a moment in the last decade as several proof-of-concept flights have shown it is indeed feasible. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How alfalfa forms root nodules without rhizobia
item.description: A research team led by professor Feng Jian at the Institute of Genetics and Developmental Biology (IGDB) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences has uncovered a cytokinin–NODULE INCEPTION (NIN) regulatory module associated with spontaneous root nodule formation in alfalfa (Medicago sativa). Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Einstein’s 120-year-old theory may be missing something big about the Big Bang
item.description: A surprising discovery by MIT and UC Santa Barbara physicists reveals that Einstein’s famous theory of particle motion misses something important when particles travel near the speed of light. Their new calculations show that heavy quarks moving through an ultra-hot plasma experience rare but unusually powerful jolts that Einstein’s traditional model cannot fully explain. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: New chemical route delivers first synthesis of plant compound with cough-suppressing potential
item.description: Neotuberostemonine, a complex plant-derived alkaloid with promising antitussive activity, has remained a challenging target for chemical synthesis for nearly 30 years. Researchers have now achieved its first total synthesis, alongside the synthesis of neostenine and the putative structure of tuberostemonine L. The findings also reveal how the nearly planar geometry of nitrogen atoms contributes to the oxidative instability of these alkaloids, offering new insights and synthetic strategies for natural-product chemistry and future drug discovery. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scientists discover a hidden gut defense that could prevent colon cancer
item.description: A common antibody in the gut may be a powerful natural defense against colon cancer, with researchers finding that mice lacking it developed more than twice as many tumors. Restoring the antibody eliminated the increased risk, revealing a promising new avenue for preventing cancer before it starts. Fuente: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Middle-aged women in England least likely to successfully quit smoking, study finds
item.description: Of nearly 8,000 women who tried to stop, only 18% of those aged 45 to 60 managed to give up Middle-aged women in England are the least likely to successfully give up smoking, according to research . Smoking is the leading cause of preventable death and illness in the UK. While overall smoking rates in England have declined in recent decades, rates in some regions have increased. About 6.75 million people smoke in England, of whom around 14% are women aged 45-60. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Anna Bawden

item.title: Quantum ingenuity can sidestep limits of conventional chips—while using commercially accessible components
item.description: For decades, computers have steadily grown faster and more powerful. Avik Dutt, an assistant professor of mechanical engineering at the University of Maryland, envisions another dramatic leap forward—one propelled by the quantum properties of light. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Laser light reveals where electrons accumulate in atomically thin semiconductor stacks
item.description: Stacking semiconductors—the chips that power phones, computers and so much more—enables quicker signal movement with less energy, but how does the process actually work? Turns out shining a literal light on the semiconducting materials can help elucidate how the electrons move in the stack, according to a multi-institutional team in Japan. The approach could help inform the development of more efficient, low-power electronics, the researchers said. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Underwater robots reveal first salp species known to live exclusively in deep sea
item.description: Salps are barrel-shaped gelatinous animals that play an important role in ocean ecosystems. More than 20 years ago, researchers observed an unfamiliar salp in the deep waters of Monterey Bay. Using specimens and data collected by MBARI's advanced underwater robots, Larry Madin, deputy director emeritus at the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution and an MBARI adjunct, recently published a detailed description of the glass salp (Vitreosalpa gemini) in the journal Marine Biodiversity. This striking species is the first salp known to live exclusively in the deep sea. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft lifts off with first foreign astronaut on board
item.description: China’s latest crewed space mission, Shenzhou-24, lifted off on Wednesday morning, taking three astronauts – including the first foreign crew member – to the Tiangong space station. In a sign of the space programme’s increasing diversity, for about a week, the station will be home to four astronauts from mainland China, one from Hong Kong and one from Pakistan. A Long March-2F rocket carrying the spacecraft blasted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in the northwestern province of... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.title: England has largest frailty gap out of 31 countries, study finds
item.description: People from lowest socioeconomic group in all countries studied had higher frailty scores than those in highest socioeconomic group England has the largest gap between higher and lower socioeconomic groups when it comes to frailty compared with 30 other countries, a major study has found. The research, led by academics at King’s College London and published in BMC Medicine, looked at levels of frailty in 71,703 people from 31 countries including England, the US, China, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Sweden, Greece, Cyprus, Latvia and Lithuania. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

Fuente: Nature.
